title: Binary search on the answer (sample lecture)
note: A short made-up lecture for the public demo. The real product works on a teacher's own recorded lectures.

transcript.text: Aaj hum binary search on the answer dekhenge. Ye tab kaam aata hai jab answer ek range mein ho aur hum check kar sakein ki koi value chalegi ya nahi.
Example: n books hain, har book ke pages diye hain, aur m students mein baantni hain. Maximum pages jo kisi ek student ko milein, use minimum karna hai.
Answer kam se kam sabse badi book jitna hoga, aur zyada se zyada saari books ke pages ka sum. Ye hamari range hai: low aur high.
Ab ek function likhte hain: possible(limit). Hum books ko order mein dete jaate hain, aur jab limit cross hone wali ho toh naya student shuru karte hain.
Agar students m se zyada lag gaye, toh ye limit bahut chhoti hai, possible false. Warna true.
Important baat: agar limit X chal jaati hai, toh X se badi har limit bhi chalegi. Isko monotonic kehte hain, aur isi wajah se binary search lag sakti hai.
Toh mid nikalo. Agar possible(mid) true hai, toh answer mid ya usse chhota ho sakta hai, high = mid. Warna low = mid + 1.
Loop tab tak chalao jab tak low < high. End mein low hi hamara answer hai.
Complexity: possible() ek baar O(n) hai, aur binary search log(sum) baar chalti hai. Total O(n log(sum)).
Common galti: mid ke liye (low + high) / 2 likhna jab values bahut badi hon. Overflow se bachne ke liye low + (high - low) / 2 likho.

parts.text: Binary search isliye lag sakti hai kyunki possible() monotonic hai: agar limit X chal jaati hai, toh usse badi har limit bhi chalegi.
Isliye answer ke ek taraf saari values fail hoti hain aur doosri taraf saari pass, aur hum beech mein boundary dhoondhte hain.
Low sabse badi book ke pages hain, kyunki wo book kisi ek student ko poori deni hi padegi.
High saari books ka sum hai: agar ek hi student sab padh le, tab bhi isse zyada nahi chahiye.
Mid ke liye low + (high - low) / 2 likho, (low + high) / 2 nahi, warna badi values par overflow ho sakta hai.
possible() ek pass mein O(n) hai, aur binary search log(sum) steps leti hai, toh total O(n log(sum)) hai.
Is sample lecture mein iska jawab nahi hai. Try: "binary search yahan kyun lag sakti hai?", "low aur high kya hain?", "overflow kaise avoid karein?"
